name: Wasabi Bridge to Bridge
summary: Wasabi Paddling Club's small boat race on Multnomah Channel from Fred's Marina. The 8-mile long course runs out past St. Johns Bridge and back past Wapato Bridge; the 4-mile short course follows the same route and turns well before St. Johns Bridge. Soup, raffle and awards after.

courses.label: Long course
courses.note: Four legs: out past St. Johns Bridge, back past Wapato Bridge to the finish.

courses.label: Short course
courses.note: Same route, turning well before St. Johns Bridge.

name: Jericho
summary: Jericho Paddling Club's small boat race in Vancouver, BC. The long course is about 12 km (7 mi) and the short course about 6 km (4 mi); the route is set on race day for conditions. All small boats welcome, PFD and leash required. Washrooms, showers and a light lunch on site. A CORA membership, bought in advance, is required.

courses.label: Long course
courses.note: About 12 km. Route set on race day for conditions.

courses.label: Short course
courses.note: About 6 km.

name: Kalama Race
summary: Mountain Home Canoe Club's small boat race on the Columbia River at Rasmussen Park, Port of Kalama. The long course (about 6.2 mi) loops counterclockwise around Sandy Island with a turn near Deer Island Beach; the short course (about 4.2 mi) loops Sandy Island and cuts back across the river. Chili lunch and awards after.

courses.label: Long course
courses.note: Around Sandy Island with a turn near the channel marker at Deer Island Beach.

courses.label: Short course
courses.note: Around Sandy Island, then across the river to the finish.

schedule: Onsite registration and canoe numbers, until 9:45
source: pnworca.org race page and host email (Kalama Race 2026), 2026

name: BBOP Small Boat Race
summary: Bellingham Bay Outrigger Paddlers' small boat race from Marine Park in Fairhaven: one 6-mile loop along the limestone shoreline past Clark's Point, through Mud Bay and back, with views of the San Juan Islands. Open to OC1, OC2, surfski, SUP and V1. Paddlers must be able to self-rescue. Hot soup around the fire pits after.

courses.label: Course
courses.note: Starts and finishes at Marine Park. Past Clark's Point, a loop through Mud Bay and back.

schedule: Hot soup at the fire pits

name: False Creek
summary: False Creek Racing Canoe Club's small boat race from the Burrard outrigger compound at Vanier Park, Vancouver, BC. Short course about 7 km (one lap), long course about 14 km (two laps). PFD and leash required, and paddlers must be able to self-rescue. A CORA membership, bought in advance, is required.

courses.label: Long course
courses.note: About 14 km, two laps.

courses.label: Short course
courses.note: About 7 km, one lap.

name: Kai Ikaika PDX
summary: Kai Ikaika and PDX Va'a Collective's small boat race on the Willamette River from the Oaks Park Community Boat House in Portland. One course of about 6.6 miles: downriver around Toe Island, upriver to red buoy #10, and back to the Oaks Park dock. Plate lunch included with entry.

courses.label: Course
courses.note: Downriver around Toe Island, upriver around red buoy #10, back to the Oaks Park dock.

name: Sand Point
summary: The Winter Series finale, hosted by Sand Point Outrigger Canoe Club at Magnuson Park. Both courses start at the Sand Point dock, head south, then turn north to Matthews Beach: the short course (5 mi) turns at the second shark buoy, the long course (9 mi) at the green channel marker. Bathrooms and showers on site.

courses.label: Long course
courses.note: South to the green channel marker, north to Matthews Beach, finish at the Sand Point dock.

courses.label: Short course
courses.note: South to the second shark buoy, north to Matthews Beach, finish at the Sand Point dock.

name: Rusty Iron
summary: Pacific Outrigger Canoe Club's race on the Columbia River at Frenchman's Bar Park, Vancouver, WA. The long course (about 8 mi) is OC6, with Mixed, Kupuna, Women's and Men's heats; the short course (about 4 mi) is open to all divisions and canoe types, including OC1 and SUP. Morning snacks included; hamburger lunch by donation.

courses.label: Long course
courses.note: OC6. Upstream about 2 miles, downstream about 4, back to the start line.

courses.label: Short course
courses.note: All divisions and canoe types. Downstream 2 miles and back.

name: Race Around the Island
summary: Columbia River Outrigger Canoe Club's OC6 race from Chinook Landing Marine Park in Fairview, OR. The long course is 10+ miles and the short course 4 to 6 miles, both open to Mixed, Women and Men from Novice through Master 70 and Unlimited. Continental breakfast provided, lunch for purchase, raffle and awards. Expect current, wing dams and ship traffic on the Columbia.

courses.label: Long course
courses.note: Open to all divisions.

courses.label: Short course
courses.note: Open to all divisions.

name: Uncle Manu K. Baker Regatta
summary: Kīkaha O Ke Kai's sprint regatta at Spanaway Lake Park: 500, 1000 and 1500 meter OC6 races on a 250 meter course with turns, plus 500 meter straightaway V1 and OC1 events. Spec OC6 canoes only. Club points awards, a raffle tent, and plate lunches for sale.
source: Host email and race info, 2026 and 2025

name: Na Poʻe O ke Kai Sprint Regatta
summary: Hui Waʻa O Wakinikona's sprint regatta on Green Lake in Seattle, run for the 27th time in 2026. Spec OC6 races on a 250 meter course with turns, plus 500 meter straightaway V1 and OC1 events. Clubs pre-register their crews. Ribbons for keiki, junior and novice events, and a raffle table.
faq: Spec OC6 races on a 250 m course with turns, and V1 and OC1 straightaway races over 500 m.

name: Silverdale Sprints
summary: Hui Heihei Waʻa's sprint regatta in Silverdale. All events run on a 250 meter course with turns for each distance. Clubs pre-register their crews by email before race day.

name: Silver Lake Sprints
summary: Hui Waʻa O Puget Sound's sprint regatta at Thornton Sullivan Park on Everett's Silver Lake. 500, 1000 and 1500 meter OC6 races on a 250 meter course with turns, plus 500 meter straightaway V1 and OC1 events. Spec OC6 canoes only in 2026. Plate lunches for sale, and club points plaques.

name: Rooster Rock Race
summary: Mountain Home Canoe Club's OC6 race on the Columbia River at Rooster Rock State Park, Corbett, OR. The long course is about 10.5 miles (women and mixed first, then men); the short course is about 5 miles, with novice, junior and youth crews encouraged. Entry includes swag, a raffle ticket and optional camping. Tacos and burritos for sale.

courses.label: Long course
courses.note: OC6. Women and mixed start first, men after.

courses.label: Short course
courses.note: OC6. Novice, junior and youth crews encouraged.

name: The Gorge Race
summary: Three Oceans' OC6 race down the Columbia River Gorge from Stevenson, WA to Drano Lake, listed at 21 miles. Women and mixed crews start first; men start half an hour after the last women's or mixed canoe finishes. Spray skirts required. Entry includes Friday and Saturday camping at the Stevenson fairgrounds. A two-person surfski and OC1 relay runs the next day.

courses.label: OC6 course
courses.note: Stevenson, WA to Drano Lake.

name: Gorge Downwind Champs
summary: A week of downwind paddling in the Columbia River Gorge for outrigger, surfski and SUP, with daily downwind shuttles, clinics and a solo race held on the day with the best wind.

name: Texwech Tayeawlh
host: Bellingham Bay Outrigger Paddlers and Autumn Rose
summary: “The Canoe Race to Eliza Island,” co-hosted by Bellingham Bay Outrigger Paddlers and Autumn Rose Canoe Club from the Lummi Nation Stommish Grounds. The 14-mile iron course runs south between Lummi and Portage islands, rounds Eliza Island and returns; the 5-mile short course is for novice and youth crews. OC6 only, unlimited or spec. Camping at the Stommish Grounds included with entry.

courses.label: Iron course
courses.note: South between Lummi and Portage islands, around Eliza Island and back.

courses.label: Short course
courses.note: Novice and youth crews only.

name: Pacific Northwest Challenge

venue.name: Sail Sand Point Marina and Beach

summary: Hosted in 2026 by Sand Point Outrigger Canoe Club and Kīkaha O Ke Kai, with a beach relay course.
source: Host emails, 2026 (information PDF attachment not read)

name: da Grind

venue.name: Alki Beach
venue.street: Alki Ave SW, between 55th and 57th Ave SW

summary: Seattle Outrigger Canoe Club's race from Alki Beach in West Seattle. The 12-mile long course circles Blake Island clockwise (OC6 and double-hull; Wahine, Kane and All-Gender). The 4-mile short course is a triangle off Alki for keiki, novices, OC1, OC2, V1, surfski and SUP. First-place Spec Wahine and Kane long-course crews go on the Da Grind trophy.

courses.label: Long course
courses.note: Clockwise around Blake Island. OC6 and double-hull.

courses.label: Short course
courses.note: Triangle off Alki: Duwamish Head to Alki Point Lighthouse. Keiki, novice and small boats.

source: seattleoutrigger.com Da Grind page and host email, 2026

name: Chicken Long Race
summary: Kīkaha O Ke Kai's small boat race along Ruston Way in Tacoma for OC1 and OC2: solo or relay over 10.5 miles, or a 5.3-mile short course (two 2.6-mile laps). Every paddler gets endless bowls of Aunty Bren's Chicken Long Rice Soup.

steps.register: Register on Webscorer as soon as possible so the host can plan how much food to cook.
steps.checkin: Registration opens at 8:00 AM at Jack Hyde Park. Mass start is at 10:00 AM.

courses.label: Solo or relay
courses.note: Relay teams change after each lap.

courses.label: Short course
courses.note: Two laps.

faq: How much does the Chicken Long Race cost?
OC1 and OC2, solo or relay.
The full course is 10.5 miles on Ruston Way. The short course is 2 laps, 5.3 miles. Each lap is 2.6 miles.
